password.description:
The existing account's password, or the one being chosen for a new
account. Which it is depends on `has_account`.

token.description: Ready to use — accepting signs you in.

output_vat.description: Credited by tax charged and owed to ZATCA. Defaults to 2100.

receivable.description: Debited by what customers owe. Defaults to 1100.

revenue.description: Credited by what was earned, excluding tax. Defaults to 4000.

otp.description:
**The six digits the taxpayer generates in the Fatoora portal.** Valid
for about an hour, used once, and never stored here.

checks_submitted.description: How many sample documents ZATCA was shown, and how many it accepted.

AddressBody.description: A Saudi national address, which is a shape rather than free text.

additional.description: The four-digit secondary number, where the address has one.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. `SA` for a business registered here.

AgedCustomerView.description: One customer's debt, split by how late it is.

customer.description: A name to show: the one the most recent invoice in this group froze.

identified.description:
Whether `key` is a customer id.

`false` means these invoices were grouped by the name they froze, so two
spellings of one buyer are two rows. Record them in `crm` and reference
them to merge.

key.description:
What this row is grouped under: a customer id, or the frozen name when
the invoices named no record.

oldest_due.description:
The due date of the oldest unpaid invoice. What a collections call opens
with.

total.description: Every bucket together, in this currency.

AmendBookable.description: The same fields without the id, which cannot change.

AmendCustomerRecord.description: The same fields without the id, which cannot change.

Amount.description:
An amount, as a client sends it.

Minor units and an explicit currency — never a decimal string, and never a
float. A client that sends `10.50` has already lost the argument about how
many decimal places the currency has.

minor.description: The amount in the currency's smallest unit. 1050 is 10.50 SAR.

unit.description: The resource picked out of the pool this line booked.

documents.description:
Documents with a tax point in this period. Invoices and credit notes on
the output side; bills on the input side.

position.description:
Where it landed in the log. A client that wants to read its own write
back passes this as `?consistent_after=`.

BookedResource.description: A resource a line takes, and how much of it.

quantity.description: Defaults to one, which is what a stylist and a chair are.

position.description:
The log position this landed at. Pass it to a read as
`?consistent_after=` to see it in the diary.

closed_before.description:
**The first instant still open.** Everything strictly before it is final
and no entry may be dated into it — not a journal entry, not an invoice's
tax point, not a credit note's.

Closing January is `2026-02-01T00:00:00Z`. Exclusive, like the VAT
return's `until`, because "closed through 31 January" is a comparison
somebody gets wrong by exactly one day.

`null` on a tenant that has never closed a period, and the way to reopen
everything.

deprecated.description: Set when the module is no longer offered. A picker should hide it.

requires_any.description: What this module needs **at least one** of. Empty for most.

request_id.description: ZATCA's `requestID`. The production request quotes the compliance one.

stage.description:
`compliance` for what an OTP buys, `production` for what a passed
compliance check buys.

serial.description: Its serial number, in hex. What ZATCA's support desk asks for.

subject.description: The certificate's subject, as one line.

skipped.description: Accounts that were already there. Installing twice is not an error.

preview.description:
Enough to show the chart before installing it, which is the
"modify before installing" story's first half — after installing, every
account is renameable and closeable.

configured.description:
`false` when nothing has been configured and these are the shipped
defaults — so a settings screen can say "using the standard chart"
rather than implying somebody chose this.

handle.description: The email address the account was registered with.

compliance_documents.description: How many sample documents the compliance checks will want afterwards.

csr.description:
**The certificate request, base64** — what goes in the `csr` field of
ZATCA's `POST /compliance`, with the OTP in an `OTP` header.

next.description: What to do with what comes back.

position.description:
The log position this landed at. Pass it to a read as
`?consistent_after=` to see it in a list.

vat_number.description: Fifteen digits, beginning and ending with 3.

icv.description:
Where it sits in the hash chain. Absent on a document issued before the
business registered, which has no place in it.

kind.description:
`standard` — cleared before the buyer gets it — or `simplified`,
reported within 24 hours.

number.description: The statutory number, which is the document's identity.

qr.description:
The base64 TLV block that goes on the printed document. Five fields
before the document is signed, nine after — the last four are the stamp.

remarks.description: Warnings on an accepted document, errors on a refused one.

source.description: The invoice it was built from.

position.description:
Where it landed in the log. A client that wants to read its own write
back passes this as `?consistent_after=`.

period.description: The period, as it identifies itself: `SAR.2026-01-01.2026-04-01`.

reference.description: ZATCA's acknowledgement, once clearance exists to produce one.

skipped.description:
Already there, and left exactly as they were. Not a failure — fitting
out twice is meant to be harmless.

signed_xml.description:
**The document as submitted**: those bytes plus the signature, the QR
and the `cac:Signature` that points at it.

stamped_xml.description:
**The document ZATCA stamped, base64** — the one a buyer must be given.
Cleared standard invoices only.

xml.description: The canonical UBL that was hashed, and what the signature covers.

currency.description: The currency every account is opened in.

accept_path.description:
Where the token goes, so a client does not have to build the URL itself
and get it subtly wrong.

On the **apex**, not the tenant's subdomain: the recipient may have no
account anywhere yet.

token.description:
**Shown once.** Pass it on however you already talk to this person.
Nothing stores it, so a lost link is re-issued rather than recovered.

tax_breakdown.description: One row per rate, which is what a Saudi tax invoice has to print.

cancelled_on.description:
Set once a credit note has cancelled it. A cancelled invoice owes
nothing, and `outstanding` says so too.

id.description: The key the client sent when issuing, and what addresses this invoice.

number.description: The statutory number. Sequential, gapless, and what the document prints.

payment_count.description:
How many payments have been recorded. The payments themselves are on
`GET /v1/sales/invoices/{invoice}`.

Not `payments`: the detail view flattens this one and adds the list, and
two shapes under one name on the same resource is a client generator's
worst afternoon.

Issued.description: A statutory document that now exists.

id.description: The key you sent, which is what addresses this document from here on.

number.description:
The statutory number, allocated here from the tenant's gapless series.
What goes on the printed document.

On a repeated request this is the number the document already has, not a
new one — the series does not move for a retry.

position.description:
Where it landed in the log. A client that wants to read its own write
back passes this as `?consistent_after=`.

vat_rate.description:
Basis points — 1500 is 15%. The rate that applied when it was issued, not
today's.

module_roles.description: Where the tenant said something different. Usually empty.

role.description:
What they are here, and in any module not listed below.

One of `owner`, `accountant`, `clerk`, `viewer`.

MessageArg.description:
A value interpolated into a message.

Typed rather than pre-formatted strings, because formatting is
locale-dependent: a count selects a plural form, a date renders differently
under a Hijri calendar, and money carries a currency whose symbol placement
varies. Handing the renderer a `String` throws away everything it needs.

oneOf.description:
Latin-script text — an identifier, a slug, a code. Bidi-isolated when
rendered into an RTL locale.

value.description:
Latin-script text — an identifier, a slug, a code. Bidi-isolated when
rendered into an RTL locale.

oneOf.description: A plain number, not a count. Does not select a plural form.

value.description: A plain number, not a count. Does not select a plural form.

oneOf.description: A quantity. Selects the plural form of the template.

value.description: A quantity. Selects the plural form of the template.

deprecated.description:
Set when the module is no longer offered, and says why. A tenant that has
it keeps it; nobody new can turn it on.

requires.description:
What this module needs underneath it, all of it. A client building a
picker needs this to grey out the impossible combinations rather than
let someone discover them.

requires_any.description: What this module needs **at least one** of. Empty for most.

stage.description:
`reserved`, `confirmed`, `arrived`, `in_service`, `completed`,
`cancelled` or `no_show`. Moving to the stage it is already in is a
no-op.

why.description: Why. Kept and shown, and it is what a cancellation reason goes in.

code.description: The account code, as the tenant numbers their chart.

currency.description:
ISO 4217. An account holds one currency, and postings in another are
refused.

kind.description:
`asset`, `liability`, `equity`, `revenue` or `expense`. Decides which
side of the account a positive balance sits on.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. `SA` for a Saudi buyer.

billed_on.description: The tax point, from their document. Not when you typed it in.

id.description:
**Your own key for this bill.** Recording the same one twice is a no-op,
which is what makes a retried request safe.

Not the supplier's number — that is `reference`, and two suppliers can
both call something `INV-001`.

reference.description:
**The supplier's own invoice number.** What a reclaim is evidenced by.
Recording the same one twice for the same supplier is refused: it would
be a duplicate claim.

account.description:
The expense or asset account this lands in. One bill routinely covers
several.

tax.description:
**The tax the supplier charged, in minor units.** Not computed here: a
reclaim is evidenced by their document, so the figure in the books has to
be the figure on it. Must be zero on anything not standard-rated.

vat.description: `standard`, `zero` or `exempt`, as the supplier treated it.

vat_rate.description:
The rate they charged, in basis points. 1500 is 15%.

Recorded rather than resolved. If it disagrees with today's statutory
rate that is a thing worth being able to see, not a thing to correct
silently.

account.description: The cash or bank account it left.

reference.description:
Your own reference — a transfer number, a cheque. Recording the same one
twice against the same bill is a no-op.

capacity.description:
How many can be held at once. One stylist, six covers at a table, eight
rooms of a type, five hundred places in a museum slot.

id.description: Your key for this resource. Declaring the same one twice is a no-op.

kind.description: `person`, `place` or `thing`. Display only — no rule branches on it.

id.description:
**Your own key for this cancellation, not the credit note's number.**
Sending the same one twice is a no-op; a different one against an invoice
that is already credited is refused.

The credit note's number is allocated here, from its own gapless series —
ZATCA numbers credit notes separately from the invoices they credit.

on.description:
When the credit is treated as happening. Usually today, not the date of
the invoice.

oneOf.description:
Where they are, as they are today. Snapshotted onto the invoice, so a
customer moving does not rewrite what was already issued.

ZATCA wants street, city and country on a standard invoice; without them
it accepts the document and warns, which is a warning that becomes a
finding at an inspection.

id.description:
The `crm` customer this is for. Optional, and checked when it is given:
an id naming no record, or an archived one, refuses the invoice.

The fields below are still yours and are still what gets printed. The
reference is for grouping; the copy is what the document says.

vat_number.description:
The buyer's VAT registration number, printed on the invoice.

**Giving one makes this a standard invoice**, which ZATCA clears before
the buyer may be given it. Leaving it out makes it a simplified one,
reported within twenty-four hours.

id.description: Your key for this customer. Registering the same one twice is refused.

kind.description: `person` or `company`. Only a company may carry a VAT number.

registered_on.description: When they became a customer. Defaults to now.

amount.description:
Minor units, **positive**: what comes off. A negative one is a charge,
which this system does not issue.

reason.description: Why, printed on the invoice — ZATCA shows it to the customer.

vat.description:
Which treatment it comes off: `standard`, `zero` or `exempt`.

**A discount reduces the tax only on what carried any.** Discounting the
standard-rated part of a mixed invoice is a different number from
discounting the exempt part, so the invoice has to say which.

id.description:
The client's own identifier for the entry. Posting the same one twice is
a no-op, which is what makes a retried request safe.

lines.description:
Must sum to zero, in one currency. An unbalanced set is a 400 carrying
the difference.

occurred_on.description: The date the business treats this as happening — not a clock reading.

filed_on.description:
The date the business treats the filing as made. Not a clock reading, for
the same reason a tax point is not one.

handle.description: The address to invite. Also the login handle they will end up with.

currency.description: ISO 4217. Every line is in this currency.

customer.description:
Copied onto the invoice as values, never as a reference. A tax invoice
is a legal document; last year's copy must not change when a customer
record does.

discounts.description:
What comes off the whole invoice, printed as its own figure rather than
folded into a smaller total.

**The tax comes off with it.** A 15 discount on a standard-rated invoice
reduces the taxable amount by 15 and the tax by 2.25 — which is why a
discount is not a negative line, and why it has to say which treatment
it comes off.

id.description:
**Your own key for this invoice, not its number.** Issuing the same one
twice is a no-op, which is what makes a retried request safe.

The invoice *number* is allocated here, from a gapless statutory series,
and comes back as `number`. Saudi law requires that sequence to have no
holes in it, which is not something a client can guarantee.

issued_on.description: The tax point. A date the business chose, not a clock reading.

lines.description: At least one line that comes to something.

net.description: Minor units, in the invoice's currency. Excluding tax.

vat.description:
`standard`, `zero` or `exempt`. The *rate* is not a client's to choose —
it is statutory, and resolved here. Zero-rated and exempt are both 0%
and mean different things on a return, so both are kept.

email.description:
Their login. If it already belongs to someone, that account gains access
rather than a second one being created for the same person.

password.description:
Chosen by the owner and handed over. An invitation flow would leave this
to the recipient — see `erp-control/src/members.rs`.

account.description: The cash or bank account it landed in.

reference.description:
The payer's or the bank's reference. Recording the same one twice against
the same invoice is a no-op.

at.description: When the booking was taken. Defaults to now.

customer.description: The `crm` record, when there is one. A walk-in has none.

customer_name.description:
What the diary prints. Frozen, so a customer changing their name next
year does not rewrite last year's calendar.

id.description:
Your key for this booking. Taking the same one twice is a no-op, and
takes no capacity the second time.

takes.description: Everything this line takes at once — the stylist *and* the chair.

until.description:
Exclusive, so a line ending at 11:00 and one starting at 11:00 are
back to back and do not clash.

what.description: What the business calls it. Never looked at by any rule here.

id.description:
The client's own identifier for the *reversing* entry. Sending the same
one twice is a no-op; a different one against an already-reversed entry
is refused.

occurred_on.description:
When the correction is treated as happening. Usually today, not the date
of the mistake — reversing into a closed period is how a filed return
stops matching the books.

vat_number.description:
Their VAT registration number. **Required if any line carries tax** —
input VAT is reclaimed against a registered supplier's tax invoice, and a
bill without one is not evidence of a reclaim.

branch.description:
The branch this unit belongs to. For a VAT group member, their own
10-digit TIN.

common_name.description: A name for this unit, unique among the taxpayer's units.

environment.description:
`sandbox`, `simulation` or `production`. **Not a default** — the only
visible difference is a string in the request, and a mistake onboards
into the wrong authority rather than failing.

issues_simplified.description: Whether it issues simplified ones — reported within 24 hours.

issues_standard.description:
Whether this unit issues standard invoices — the ones cleared before the
buyer gets them.

serial.description: This unit's serial number, unique per taxpayer.

live.description: Whether it can clear and report real invoices.

reached.description: Which stages this tenant has credentials for: `compliance`, `production`.

closes_at.description:
Minutes past local midnight, exclusive. `1020` is 17:00, and a booking
may run right up to it.

days.description: 1 to 31. Empty means every day of the month.

from.description: The first day these hours apply. Absent means they always have.

months.description: 1 is January. Empty means every month.

until.description: The last day, **inclusive**. Absent means they always will.

weekdays.description: 1 is Monday, 7 is Sunday. Empty means every day of the week.

Paged_AgedCustomerView.description:
One page of a list, and where the next one starts.

# Why every list is shaped like this

Because the alternative was a bare array that stopped at 200 and said
nothing. A tenant with 201 invoices saw 200 and had no way to tell — the
response looked exactly like a complete one, which is the worst shape a bug
can have.

`next` absent means **the list ended**. Present means pass it back as
`?after=` to continue.

items.description: One customer's debt, split by how late it is.

customer.description: A name to show: the one the most recent invoice in this group froze.

identified.description:
Whether `key` is a customer id.

`false` means these invoices were grouped by the name they froze, so two
spellings of one buyer are two rows. Record them in `crm` and reference
them to merge.

key.description:
What this row is grouped under: a customer id, or the frozen name when
the invoices named no record.

oldest_due.description:
The due date of the oldest unpaid invoice. What a collections call opens
with.

total.description: Every bucket together, in this currency.

next.description:
Pass back as `?after=` for the next page. Absent when there are no more.

Opaque: what is in it is the query's business, and a client that parsed
one would break the day a list is ordered differently.

PaymentRecorded.description:
Something recorded against a document, which is not a document itself.

A payment carries no statutory number: the invoice it settles is the numbered
thing, and a receipt references that.

id.description: The invoice it was recorded against.

company.description:
What you are being invited to, and as what. A link that does not say is
a link people accept without reading.

has_account.description:
`true` when that address already has an account here — so the form asks
for the existing password rather than offering to choose a new one.

example.detail: Those login details are not right. Please try again.
example.title: Unauthorized

args.description:
The values the message names, typed — which account, which module, how
much was outstanding. A client that renders its own sentence reads these
instead of parsing `detail`. Absent when the message takes none.

code.description: The stable identifier. Branch on this, never on `detail`.

detail.description: The message in the caller's language, chosen by `Accept-Language`.

type.description:
`https://errors.erp.example/` followed by the code. Stable, and a place
to look it up — see `docs/ERRORS.md` for every code this API can answer
with.

standard.description:
The standard rate in **basis points**. 1500 is 15% (Saudi Arabia), 500
is 5% (the UAE).

Zero-rated and exempt are 0% by definition and not configurable — a
jurisdiction that taxed an exempt supply would not call it exempt.

Applies to invoices issued **from now on**. Every document already issued
carries the rate it was issued under, so changing this cannot restate a
filed return.

effective_from.description:
When the business treats the registration as effective. Not a clock
reading, for the same reason a tax point is not one.

identifier.description: The number in that register — the commercial registration, usually.

name.description:
**The legal name, in Arabic** — it is what the invoice says, because the
invoice is an Arabic document.

name_latin.description: The same name in Latin script, for screens. Never sent to ZATCA.

vat_number.description: Fifteen digits, beginning and ending with `3`.

lines.description:
The whole set, replacing what was there. Assignments are dropped: a
line that moved has to be given a unit again at its new hour.

unit.description: The unit picked out of the pool, once one has been.

input.description:
What was paid on purchases, and the reclaimable part of it. Empty when
the tenant has no purchases module.

output.description:
What was charged on sales, net of credit notes with a tax point in this
period. Empty when the tenant has no sales module.

payable.description:
**The number that gets paid, or reclaimed.** Output tax less input tax;
negative means ZATCA owes the business.

token.description: Ready to use — confirming logs you in.

email.description:
The first user's login. A confirmation goes here, and nothing is created
until it comes back.

modules.description:
Modules to start with. Unknown names are refused rather than ignored, so
a typo is not a silently missing feature discovered at month end.

slug.description: The tenant's name in URLs. 2–50 characters.

SignupRequested.description:
What a request produced, which is deliberately not much.

No token, and no identifier for the pending request. Both would be a way to
confirm without the mailbox, which is the whole thing this endpoint exists
to require. What comes back is what a page needs to say "check your email"
and to know when the link stops working.

email.description:
Where the confirmation went. Echoed back lowercased and trimmed, which
is the form it was stored in.

awaiting_clearance.description:
**Standard invoices not yet cleared.** Not late — a standard invoice is
cleared before issue — but documents the buyer must not have yet.

chain_length.description: How many documents are in the chain.

counts.description:
How many documents are in each state: `unregistered`, `pending`,
`cleared`, `reported`, `refused`.

overdue.description:
**Simplified invoices past their 24 hours and still not reported.** The
number an inspection asks about.

registered.description:
Whether there is a registration at all. Nothing can be cleared or
reported without one, so everything else here is moot until it is true.

unsigned.description:
**Documents with no signature yet.** They can be neither submitted nor
printed with a phase-two QR, so this is the number that says a business
is not really live whatever else is true.

modules.description:
The modules this tenant has turned on. A route belonging to any other
module answers 404 here.

role.description:
What the caller may do here, so a client can hide what it must not
offer. The server refuses regardless — this is for the buttons.

One of `owner`, `accountant`, `clerk`, `viewer`.

hours.description:
Every window this resource is offered in. **An empty list means always**,
which is what a hotel room and a museum slot want.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday as 1. Empty means every day.

TradeResourceView.description: One thing a trade would declare.

capacity.description:

info.description:
A multi-tenant ERP. Every tenant has its own database; every write is an event; every read model is derived and can be rebuilt.

## Authentication

`POST /v1/sessions` returns a bearer token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Operations documented without the `session` requirement are deliberately open — the module catalogue and the chart-of-accounts catalogue are product information a signup form needs before anyone has an account, and an invitation's token *is* its credential.

## Errors

Every failure is `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) carrying a stable `code`. **Branch on the code, never on `detail`**, which is prose in whichever language the request asked for. `args` carries the values the message names, typed, so a client can render its own sentence. `docs/ERRORS.md` lists every code.

Two exceptions, and they are the honest kind: **413** (a body over 1 MB) and **504** (a request still running after 30 seconds) are refused at the edge, before anything in this document runs, and carry no body at all. Every operation below can answer either.

## Language

`Accept-Language` is honoured on every response, including failures. Arabic and English are first-class; anything else falls back to English rather than failing.

## Reading your own write

Read models are driven by a worker, so a read taken immediately after a write can legitimately not see it. Every write returns the log `position` it landed at; pass it back as `?consistent_after=<position>` and the read waits for the projection to reach it. Without it, reads are served as they are.

## Money

Minor units and an explicit currency, never a decimal string and never a float. `{ "minor": 1050, "currency": "SAR" }` is 10.50 SAR.

post.description:
Four calls to ZATCA, in the order it requires:

1. a key pair and a certificate request, generated here,
2. `POST /compliance` with the OTP — the compliance certificate,
3. `POST /compliance/invoices` — one signed sample of every document type
   this unit declared, which ZATCA must accept before it will go further,
4. `POST /production/csids` — the certificate that clears real invoices.

**Nothing is stored unless the step that produced it succeeded**, and the
private key is sealed before the first call, so a certificate is never issued
against a key this system no longer has.

If the compliance samples are refused, that is **this software's problem, not
the caller's** — the samples are generated here — and it answers 502 with
what ZATCA said.
